## 07 — Complete slanted marginal note and neighbouring letter context

The rotated note shows introduire la partition: the opening word ends in a short rising r-like connector and final curved e, supporting introduire, medium, choosing A/B and C witness over reader C's added ending qualification and H introduisons. The partition letter has a high top and two legs with a curved right return; retain \unsure{\Pi|\pi}_j, medium, original C R04 first part retained. The heavy crossed form immediately before E_j has Sigma-like diagonal and bottom strokes, but its overlay remains crowded; retain \deleted{\unsure{\Sigma}}E_j, low, R04 second part retained. Retain the complete formula and closing brace from A's margin source. In this deliberately wider first crop, the short wedge reported by B after the brace is visibly the thick lower-left return of the S in neighbouring Soit: its loop/stem continues into that word on the main text line. Select A/C's attachment; represent it once through Soit, with a noncount component/coverage row, rather than a second free-standing margin glyph. Its attachment is medium confidence. H's terminal ill placeholder has no separately legible word following the note's closing brace in this crop. Preserve the reader disagreement about its possible referent; group the omitted crossed predecessor and the unspecified H placeholder under one marginal parent H difference, low, without claiming an exact positional identity for H's placeholder. Do not count the predecessor and placeholder twice. The adjacent Considerons and cancelled lower word are incidental context only; their accent/word decisions remain reserved for their planned crops.

root_decision_sources.literal_tex:
## 10 — Cancelled and live definie after de X

Viewed `readers/017/A/06_cancelled_definie.png` once.

The cancelled word has a looped d, low e, tall f with descending return, followed by the short i/n/i/e sequence. Resolve original C R05 to \deleted{definie}, medium, selecting A/B. Its visible detached point belongs over a later i; the area over the e is blank. Preserve the unaccented spelling in both this cancelled word and the immediately following live definie, medium. Reader C's accented versions and witness C/H's accented versions are recorded as the alternatives rejected at these two separate word positions. The cancelled wording is one cluster (1C/1H); the live word's accent is a second cluster (1C/1H). The entire old word is crossed by one long horizontal stroke, and the following word remains live.

## 11 — Crossed predecessor under the main E_j

Viewed `readers/017/A/07_first_E_predecessor.png` once.

The overlaid main E_j contains an extra diagonal through its centre and lower angular return supporting a previous Sigma. root_decision_sources.literal_tex:
## 12 — Short et and the live intersection word

Viewed `readers/017/A/08_intersection_start.png` once.

At the left a small e loop and tall t-like stem support et, but the heavy horizontal connection through it merges into the following word and does not settle whether that short word is cancelled. Select reader C's complete-state \unsure{\deleted{et}|et}, low. Original C R06 first part therefore has et letters resolved and cancellation state qualified; keep those components explicit under the same source row, one C physical-cluster difference for the new state qualification. The following connected sequence supports intersection, and its t/i/o/n ending is clear. The initial vertical/cursive entry is crowded by the preceding strokes; retain local case uncertainty as \unsure{intersection|Intersection}, low, combining B/C's lower-case primary with A's capital alternative. The word identity is supported but the original C R06 word doubt remains locally qualified, 0C for that component. Preserve this live word once on the baseline. H's struck intersection plus inserted intersection is replaced by the short et state cluster followed by the single live word; count one H parent difference across these connected state/word spans, with the second component noncount.

Viewed `crops/scan017_first_Pi_guide.png` once.

The raised Pi_J lies above de. A separate guide curves from a low left start upward, runs shallowly rightward above de and ends in a short upward hook. Select A's complete G03 group, including the inserted Pi_J and its one live de node, fixed rectangle, anchors and exact draw command. The final short straight return in A's path represents the visible end hook. Count the guide/placement graphic once, medium, 1C/1H; the agreed Pi_J glyph and live de are coverage components. Do not repeat de outside the selected group. The letter and guide retain the manuscript hand attribution shared by the readers.

root_decision_sources.literal_tex:
## 10 — Cancelled and live definie after de X

Viewed `readers/017/A/06_cancelled_definie.png` once.

The cancelled word has a looped d, low e, tall f with descending return, followed by the short i/n/i/e sequence. Resolve original C R05 to \deleted{definie}, medium, selecting A/B. Its visible detached point belongs over a later i; the area over the e is blank. Preserve the unaccented spelling in both this cancelled word and the immediately following live definie, medium. Reader C's accented versions and witness C/H's accented versions are recorded as the alternatives rejected at these two separate word positions. The cancelled wording is one cluster (1C/1H); the live word's accent is a second cluster (1C/1H). The entire old word is crossed by one long horizontal stroke, and the following word remains live.

## 11 — Crossed predecessor under the main E_j

Viewed `readers/017/A/07_first_E_predecessor.png` once.

The overlaid main E_j contains an extra diagonal through its centre and lower angular return supporting a previous Sigma. Several strokes coincide with the E and the cancellation, so the earlier glyph remains qualified. Select reader C's \deleted{\unsure{\Sigma}}E_j, low, over A/B's firm predecessor. Original C R07 first part explicitly qualified this locus although its TeX printed a firm Sigma; retain that source doubt (0C), and record H's omitted old glyph once (1H). Original C R06 first part therefore has et letters resolved and cancellation state qualified; keep those components explicit under the same source row, one C physical-cluster difference for the new state qualification. The following connected sequence supports intersection, and its t/i/o/n ending is clear. The initial vertical/cursive entry is crowded by the preceding strokes; retain local case uncertainty as \unsure{intersection|Intersection}, low, combining B/C's lower-case primary with A's capital alternative. The word identity is supported but the original C R06 word doubt remains locally qualified, 0C for that component. Preserve this live word once on the baseline. H's struck intersection plus inserted intersection is replaced by the short et state cluster followed by the single live word; count one H parent difference across these connected state/word spans, with the second component noncount.

## 01 — Opening cancelled clause and raised replacement

Viewed `readers/017/A/01_upper_correction.png` once.

The cancelled subject has a left upright and overlapping horizontal/diagonal passes; E_i remains the leading reading, but the cancellation does not settle the Sigma_i alternative. Select B's \unsure{E_i|\Sigma_i}, low, original C R01 subject retained, 0C. The following short verb remains \unsure{est|soit}, low: the connected/cancelled stems do not settle the alternative; the extra named alternative retains C's existing uncertainty, 0C. The adjective's short r opening, open rounded middle and final re favour rare; resolve that part of R01 to rare, medium (A/C), 1C. The X is followed by a distinct dark point inside the cancelled clause; preserve X. (H omission, high). Above the deletion the replacement on ait is visibly raised, agreeing with all three insertion states (H placement, high). The parenthesis begins with the connected s and dotted i of si, not H's où; select si, high. No mathematical expectation was used. A.workflow: Brief read first; current UTC start was then recorded before packet/image reading. Whole scan opened once for layout, half a once, half b once. Sixteen initial distinct tight crops, three later previously uncropped accent loci, and one final previously uncropped detached-mark locus were each displayed once. The final mark crop followed the initial source-only structural check. No successfully viewed image or decided target was reopened. No crop retry occurred.
A.coordinates: Full scan is 1685x2363. Half a is 1685x1261 and starts at full y=0. Half b is 1685x1262; bottom alignment yields full y=half-b y+1101, using 2363-1262. Report full boxes use upper-left origin and [left,top,right,bottom]. Unrotated crop display coordinates use x_full=left+x_display*(right-left)/2600 and y_full=top+y_display*(bottom-top)/output_height. These maps locate hand-estimated graphical anchors. The rotated marginal crop was used for reading without a computed inverse rotation.
A.graphics: G01 and G08 each contain two literal draw paths. G02,G03,G04,G07,G09,G10 each contain one. G11 contains two separate fill paths. G05 is represented once by a qualified prime/dot candidate, and G06 once by a qualified baseline point. Every insertion-guide path appearing in reading.tex has its own difference and inventory item. Local drawing origins, rectangles, coordinate units, baselines and zero-separation base-west text anchors are declared in TeX; font extents are not asserted to coincide with source boxes.

No target was recropped.
